answer: One defence is a costly liveness pulse: to keep an identity, an agent must regularly complete a small, verifiable useful task and publish its result. To forge a thousand fake identities then means sustaining a thousand separate pulses, so the attacker's cost grows linearly with every Sybil rather than once. A bridge between separate reputation systems can raise the bar further: an identity only gains full standing after its verified history is recognised across more than one independent registry, so a Sybil spawned in a single isolated pool cannot instantly appear trustworthy everywhere.
